name: Baby Lincoln Falls
text: [overview] A small climb beside the Granite Lake approach trail, near a good camp on Granite Creek: about 30 ft of WI2-3 ice, then 30 ft of steep snowfield up to a sturdy belay tree.

name: All in Moderation
text: [approach] The route begins in the 4th of July Couloir and leaves it about a third of the way up, above the first black rocks, into an obvious left-leaning snow gully.

name: Grinnell Falls
text: [overview] If the ice is not cooperating, take the snow gully further left (WI2) to the capstone, Grinnell Falls Proper, which offers several flows from WI5 on the left to WI2 on the right.
[overview] Above, low-angle snow gives a running belay all the way to the lake above (Upper Grinnell).
[detailed_rack] Ice screws (about half a standard set), a few runners, and a picket for snow.
[approach] The Many Glacier road is closed in winter, so reaching Grinnell Lake is a multi-day trip on skis or snowshoes (sled or bike where the road allows);

name: Splash Cats' Eating Disorder
text: [approach] The Many Glacier road is closed in winter, so the trip is a long ski or snowshoe in.
[descent_text] Build an anchor at the trees above the ice, then walk off down the Grinnell Glacier Trail.

name: Six Pack of Beer & Nothing to Do

[overview] Traverse left on a snowy ledge, up a rightward runnel to the lower snowfield, then up-left to a couloir zigzagging right to the band of rock higher up.

name: The Stumbling Stone
text: [approach] Stay to climber's right of the feature called Thunderdome and follow the obvious gully and snow slope.

name: Northwest Chimney Route
text: [overview] over rock that is surprisingly solid for Glacier, reaching a belay/rappel station on the right (in 2020: a tri-cam and two good pitons).

name: If I Had A Hammer
text: [overview] Early season may need an ice axe and crampons.
[descent_text] Steep snow can fill this ground, calling for an ice axe and sometimes crampons.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Get going early, since cornices can break from the summit ridge above.
[overview] Steep neve and WI3 for several pitches lead to a rock band, where two pitches of M4-5, and maybe one M6 move, follow.
[overview] Work left (east) when possible to get out from beneath the 40' cornices 800' above, then go 700' straight up more steep neve.
[approach] The face carries cornices on the summit ridge above, which is why parties start early.

name: West Ridge
text: [overview] Expect sweeping range views, huge cornices and mushroom-shaped snow.
[approach] The route follows the west ridge, which holds snow gendarmes and large cornices, so check the avalanche forecast.

name: Lunar Arete
text: [approach] From the south end of the lake, skirt the east shore and aim for the snow at the foot of the arete, then climb the steep permanent snowfield, which steepens to about 50 degrees near its top, to the base of the rock.
[descent_text] The South Slopes route is shorter but can hold alpine ice in the snowfield and has very loose fourth-class terrain beside it.

name: Northeast Couloir
text: [overview] some parties mention a big cornice near the end.
[overview] Descend by downclimbing the couloir until glissading works, or take the rocky ridges, with care on loose, exposed rock.
[approach] The couloir is steep snow, so check the avalanche forecast.
[descent_text] Usually descend by downclimbing the steep couloir until the slope eases enough to glissade, depending on conditions.

name: Waves of Emotion
text: [overview] Start on the toe by the snowfield's low point, right of The Fellowship.
